author: garyrong
content:
Hey, sorry for the late reply, I was off for the past two days. Let me provide a bit more context on EIP-7610.

This EIP was drafted by Martin and me two years ago. The intention was to define the expected behavior for the edge case where a deployment destination has a zero nonce, empty code, but non-empty storage. This is theoretically possible, but in practice it is gated by a 160-bit hash collision (very hard to trigger).

The ultimate solution is to modify these 28 special accounts through an irregular state transition. At the time, we thought the **Verkle Transition** would be the best opportunity to do so, which is essentially the approach described in EIP-8253. I agree that EIP-7610 is not the ideal solution, but it is cheap enough to deploy retroactively without requiring an irregular state transition and a hardfork. That's the main reason we proposed it.

Now that it is being proposed for Amsterdam, if you guys think EIP-8253 is likely to be included shortly afterward in Bogota, *I'm fine with removing EIP-7610 from Amsterdam*. The tradeoff is during the period between these two forks, the behavior of this edge case would remain undefined.

Regarding L2 compatibility, I know Optimism has a large number of accounts that are eligible deployment destinations despite having non-empty storage, so deploying EIP-8253 would be a significant burden for them. My personal view is that, for this state-specific EIP, we should focus only on Ethereum mainnet. L2s may need to figure out alternative approaches that better fit their own state.

We can discuss it in the Next ACDT tomorrow.

cc <@508125616940515329>

author: jochembrouwer
content:
We should still ship EIP-7610 in Glamsterdam to signal to other chains that without EIP-7610 the behavior is undefined and also clearly unwanted. In case of a collission you now enter a contract where there is storage (so this storage would technically be available in initcode, where SLOADs return nonzero even if initcode did not set storage). 
We could update EIP-7610 to reflect these accounts on L1, with the note that L2s have to find their own way to deal with these accounts (for instance, creating this map Geth created for L1, but now for that specific L2). I have no strong opinion on this.
In Hegota, we ship EIP-8253 so we get rid of these type of accounts and also of the unspecified behavior.
By keeping EIP-7610 in Glamsterdam we signal that we are dealing with this situation. By removing it there is the risk that EIP-8253 does not get shipped in Hegota, and then we are delaying this again. EIP-7610 signals that we want to take care of this situation.

I do not see how BALs break EIP-7610. There are account reads in BALs, the reads do not specify what is read (nonce, balance, code, storage root). I therefore do not see what changes here. 

(I champion EIP-8253 to ensure this gets shipped in Hegota, so we get rid of these type of accounts forever. We then don't have to deal with it in clients anymore, plus also some EIPs do not have to deal with these accounts by specifying the behavior for those)

author: jochembrouwer
content: EIP-7610 could also be rebranded with the guarantee (or drop a note about this): a contract always starts with empty storage (in initcode)

author: jochembrouwer
content:
If we use the rule "a contract always starts with empty storage", then we must include EIP-7610 with BALs, otherwise on collission we need to delete the storage trie first (which means we now have unbounded operatoin).
We could also spec that we do *not* wipe the storage, but this now creates the theoretical possibility for a contract to start with non-empty storage in it's initcode.
I believe we must spec this undefined behavior which is why we should ship EIP-7610 in Glamsterdam. It specs that contracts start with empty storage in initcode implicitly via the storage root check.
